problem_addressed: In July 2020 the e-Governance Agency named resistance from data owners, inconsistent data and incompatible systems as obstacles to data exchange. The Court of Accounts, restating its 2020 audit of public sector information systems, says a large part of those systems do not exchange information. The Commission reports read do not name MConnect or its underuse; the 2025 report asks only for stronger interoperability between verification systems and state registries.
reform_or_mechanism: MConnect was piloted from 2014 to 2018, and Law 142/2018 defines how data exchange happens through it. Amendments effective on 18 January 2021 wrote into Article 6 of that law the duty not to ask for documents available through the platform, and added fines and temporary disqualification from a post to the Code of Contraventions. The operator also states a free data rule between public participants, a duty on participants to make their data sets available, and a designed route for participants with no information system.
how_implemented: The operator reports 480+ public and private institutions connected, 2.6+ million requests a day and 600 million exchanges in total, under 2024 figures on its own page. The only independent evidence is the Court of Accounts follow-up of September 2024, which concerns public sector information systems and not MConnect as such. It reports that connecting one named system was still under analysis, and that it was shown no evidence that a planned exchange between two systems was carried out or works. No source read says that any fine or disqualification has been applied.
evidence_of_results: No outcome evidence found. Searched: the operator's MConnect page, its 2021 notice and 2025 project summary, the Commission 2024 and 2025 reports, the 2024 Interoperable Europe supporting document and the Court of Accounts follow-up. None measures use by institutions over time, documents no longer requested, or any effect of the 2021 amendments.
limitations_of_evidence: Every use figure is the operator's own, is machine translated, combines public and private bodies and has no earlier figure to compare with. The two volume figures do not reconcile: 2.6 million a day would pass 600 million in about 230 days, so they may count different things. The Court of Accounts audit of MConnect (MDA-GOV-2021-001) returned HTTP 403 and the MConnect statistics dataset returned 404, so neither is evidence here, and the audit wording seen only in search excerpts at country selection is not used (LIM-0028).
practical_lesson_for_north_macedonia: North Macedonia already has a legal obligation to use its platform (MKD-GOV-2022-004-0050), and its 2023 strategy says competence to inspect laws on ICT use is not established (MKD-GOV-2023-002-0029), so Moldova's sanctions are the closest parallel in these cases. The evidence stops at the text of the law: it does not show that the sanctions were applied or that they raised use. The most this case supports is that a sanction in law is an untested mechanism here, and that a connection count, such as 480+, does not show regular use.
transferable: The underlying mechanism, a duty on officials and bodies backed by a personal sanction, could be written into comparable administrative law. The designed route for participants with no system speaks to the same barrier as North Macedonia's lack of communications software (MKD-EU-2023-001-0153), but the only source is a 2020 design slide.
not_transferable: Moldova's connection count includes private bodies and has no activity threshold, so it cannot be set against North Macedonia's 58 connected and 33 active institutions (MKD-GOV-2025-004-0064). North Macedonia's stated barriers are IT staff, software, coordination and process change (MKD-GOV-2025-004-0065), which a sanction does not itself supply. In the reports read, the Commission does not raise platform underuse for Moldova, whereas in North Macedonia data exchange sits in a Reform Agenda payment condition (MKD-EU-2024-007-0016).
can_be_attributed: No result can be attributed to the 2021 amendments or to MConnect. It can be said only that the legal duties and sanctions exist on paper, as the operator's notice states them.
cannot_be_attributed: The 480+ connections and the 2.6+ million daily requests cannot be attributed to the duty, the sanctions or the free data rule, because no earlier figure exists in the evidence and nothing shows a sanction was applied. The Commission's and Interoperable Europe's general remarks do not address the amendments.
description: Moldova put a legal duty and sanctions behind MConnect from January 2021, and the operator reports high volumes, but no evidence shows that the sanctions were applied or what changed use. The Court of Accounts audit of MConnect was blocked and is a recorded gap.

problem_addressed: The Ministry describes citizens acting as couriers between administrations, collecting certificates from several counters. WeBER reports that administrative data are still not consistently shared, with around 53 to 54% of surveyed citizens saying they had to submit documents the state already held the last time they requested a service. The Commission says further service delivery developments are hampered by fragmented responsibilities and the lack of a dedicated coordination system, without tying this to the Bus.
reform_or_mechanism: The Law on General Administrative Procedure of 2016 obliges administrations to exchange data and documents from official records among themselves, and introduced the once-only principle. The e-ZUP system was established in June 2017 on the basis of that law and is now the Government Service Bus. An improved Bus was launched in December 2023, and the Commission says an interoperability framework is in place.
how_implemented: The Commission states in 2024 and 2025 that more databases are connected to the Bus, with no number and no volume of use. The Ministry reports more than 170 million data exchanged in six years, and on an undated page 18 databases of eight institutions. WeBER found the once-only principle implemented in a sample of seven services, except property registration, where it is unclear whether it is or can be applied. The report does not name the Bus or eZUP.
evidence_of_results: The Ministry claims nearly 500,000 citizen hours and about RSD 20 million saved in the first year, and describes eEnrolment as removing paper documents, with no method given. WeBER's February 2025 survey (N = 1006) found around 53 to 54% had to submit documents already held by the state at their last request, while 68% agreed in general terms that they are not required to. No source gives use of the Bus by institution over time.
limitations_of_evidence: The savings are a Ministry self-report with no comparison group, and they describe a period before the run's window (flagged out_of_window). The survey measures citizen perception at one date, is not linked to any database or service, and sits against the 3/3 score on sampled services. The 170 million figure is a volume of exchange and is treated here as implementation, although second-pass classification noted it as outcome. WeBER is EU-funded with the Ministry named as a project associate.
practical_lesson_for_north_macedonia: Serbia does not show what raises institutional use, because no source measures it. It shows that a legal duty and a live exchange system, with more databases connected, can sit alongside about half of surveyed citizens reporting they were still asked for documents. This is relevant to North Macedonia's conflict between telling the screening that once-only is applied and its Reform Agenda saying institutions do not gather evidence ex officio (MKD-EU-2023-003-0029, MKD-GOV-2024-001-0097). The lesson goes no further than this: connection and sample compliance do not settle whether evidence is obtained ex officio.
transferable: The mechanism of a procedural duty to exchange data, with a central system built on it, matches North Macedonia's own Law on General Administrative Procedure and platform. WeBER's measures, a citizen survey on documents resubmitted alongside a review of sampled services, could be applied wherever the same monitor runs; the Serbian and Montenegrin reports share the indicators.
not_transferable: North Macedonia's stated problem is institutions not using the platform, while Serbia's evidence is on the citizen side and does not name the platform. The undated 18 databases of eight institutions cannot be set against North Macedonia's 58 connected and 33 active institutions, because they count different things. No source read connects Serbia's position to its accession stage or to an EU payment condition on data exchange, so that difference is not tested.
can_be_attributed: The sequence of law first and system second can be stated, since the Ministry says e-ZUP was established on the basis of the 2016 law. The Ministry itself attributes the first-year savings to e-ZUP, but this is its claim and not a verified result.
cannot_be_attributed: The rise in connected databases cannot be attributed to the 2023 improved Bus or to the legal duty: the Commission gives no cause and no number. The survey result cannot be attributed to the Bus in either direction, because the report does not name it and there is no baseline.
description: Serbia has a 2016 legal duty to exchange data and a Bus to which the Commission says more databases are connected, but no source measures use by institutions. Around half of surveyed citizens still report being asked for documents the state holds.

problem_addressed: The Commission says in 2024 and 2025 that the Law on Administrative Procedure is not consistently implemented, notably on once-only and electronic communication, and that integrating all public registers into the exchange system is incomplete. The Ministry names insufficient data available through web services and slow settling of legal and organisational preconditions as the obstacles to full interoperability. Its official also says some public bodies are not meeting their obligations under the Law on Electronic Administration, and citizens contact institutions one by one.
reform_or_mechanism: The Ministry of Public Administration established JSERP, a single system for electronic data exchange between state bodies, and a Metaregister. A new X-Road platform has since been established, according to a government text of 2026. The Law on Electronic Government, the once-only principle and the Reform Agenda sit around it, and expanding JSERP to connect all registers is proposed in the 2026 to 2029 open government plan.
how_implemented: Government reporting gives 21 institutions with access in both the 2024 report and the 2026 text, while active register pairs rose from 18 to 37, and 8 million queries in 2024. The share of catalogue e-services that can draw on more than one register in one query was 0 in 2023 and 2024, against a 10% target. The Commission reports some progress on data exchange in 2024 and incomplete register integration in 2025. Strengthening the information society inspection was not achieved, which an official puts down to delays in the staffing plan.
evidence_of_results: The Ministry claims that JSERP has significantly improved electronic service delivery, with no figure. The Institute Alternative survey of February 2025 (1010 citizens) found 53.6% aware they need not provide documents the state holds and 19.9% reporting once-only in practice, and scores citizen experience 0/2. These concern the once-only principle, and no source links them to JSERP.
limitations_of_evidence: All use figures are government self-reports, machine translated and capped at Medium. The base of the 19.9% is unclear, and the 3/3 score for practice rests on published lists of documents, not on observed exchange. The Metaregister figures of 45, 170+ and 265 may count different things and are not a trend. The SIGMA finding on special laws reaches us second-hand, since SIGMA 2024 was blocked (LIM-0028), and a 2023 cybersecurity crisis delayed digital services, which further clouds any before and after reading.
practical_lesson_for_north_macedonia: Montenegro has the only use series in these cases: active register pairs doubled while institutions with access stayed at 21, and no source says why, although the X-Road platform was introduced in between. Its stated obstacles, data not available through web services and slow settling of legal and organisational preconditions, resemble North Macedonia's need to digitalise registers, change processes and integrate software (MKD-GOV-2025-004-0065). The stalled inspection parallels North Macedonia's missing inspection competence (MKD-GOV-2023-002-0029), but it shows the lever was not pulled, not that it would work. The case supports the point that counts of connected institutions and of active exchanges can move separately.
transferable: The underlying mechanism, a central exchange system with a catalogue of registers and a count of active pairs, is close to North Macedonia's platform and could be measured the same way. The stated preconditions, data available through web services and settled legal and organisational arrangements, are institutional rather than specific to Montenegro.
not_transferable: Montenegro's 21 institutions have access to a platform being rebuilt, whereas North Macedonia's audit refers to connecting around 1,300 institutions (MKD-GOV-2022-004-0051) and its platform has been in place since 2015 (MKD-EU-2023-003-0040), so scale and starting point differ. The active register pair is not the same measure as North Macedonia's active institution (MKD-GOV-2025-004-0186). Both countries have a Reform Agenda, but Montenegro's is cited only in a Commission recommendation, and no source says how it affected use.
can_be_attributed: No rise in use can be attributed to any reform on this evidence. It can be stated that the official links the stalled inspection to delays in the staffing plan, as that official's view, not a verified finding.
cannot_be_attributed: The rise from 18 to 37 pairs cannot be attributed to X-Road, the legal duties or the Reform Agenda, because no source gives a cause and both figures are self-reported. The Ministry's claim that services improved through JSERP cannot be accepted as a result, and it sits awkwardly with 0% of e-services querying more than one register. The survey result cannot be attributed to JSERP.
description: Montenegro's register pairs in active exchange rose from 18 to 37 while institutions with access stayed at 21, on government figures with no stated cause. The Commission still finds register integration and once-only incomplete, and strengthening the inspection stalled on staffing.
